q: In IUPAC nomenclature, the carbonyl carbon of an aldehyde (-CHO group) is always numbered as
why: The CHO carbon is given the lowest possible locant, C1, by IUPAC convention.

q: Rosenmund reduction of an acid chloride (R-COCl) with H2/Pd-BaSO4 gives
why: Rosenmund reduction selectively reduces acid chlorides to aldehydes, stopping before the alcohol stage.

q: In nucleophilic addition to carbonyl compounds, the reactivity order is generally
why: Fewer and less bulky alkyl groups on the carbonyl carbon of HCHO make it most electrophilic and reactive.

q: Aldol condensation requires the starting carbonyl compound to have at least one
why: Dilute base removes an alpha-hydrogen to form the carbanion (enolate) needed to attack another carbonyl molecule.

q: 2 CH3CHO with dilute NaOH gives an aldol product that, on heating, loses water to form
why: The beta-hydroxy aldehyde (3-hydroxybutanal) dehydrates on heating to the alpha,beta-unsaturated but-2-enal.

q: Tollens' reagent gives a bright silver mirror with
why: Tollens' reagent (ammoniacal AgNO3) oxidises aldehydes to carboxylic acids, depositing metallic silver; ketones do not react.

q: A compound gives a positive iodoform test. This confirms the presence of a
why: The iodoform test with I2/NaOH gives yellow CHI3 specifically from methyl ketones or compounds oxidisable to them.

q: Carboxylic acids are much more acidic than alcohols mainly because
o: Carboxylic acids have a higher boiling point
The carboxylate ion is resonance stabilised equally over two oxygens
why: The negative charge in R-COO- is delocalised equally between two oxygen atoms by resonance, stabilising the ion strongly.

q: Which test distinguishes a carboxylic acid from a phenol by producing effervescence?
why: Carboxylic acids react with NaHCO3 releasing CO2 gas (effervescence); phenols, being weaker acids, do not react.

q: In the HVZ reaction, CH3COOH with Cl2 in presence of red phosphorus gives
why: Red phosphorus catalyses substitution of an alpha-hydrogen by chlorine, giving chloroacetic acid.
